claims.text: The starting material is an equiatomic or near-equiatomic mixture of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti elemental powders.
Conventional casting of CoCrFeNiTi produces a porous, soft, homogeneous single-phase FCC structure.
Cast CoCrFeNiTi has hardness below 200 HV.
High-energy ball milling for 20–40 hours followed by SPS at 900–1000 K, heating above 100 K/min, and holding below 5 minutes is the proposed processing regime.
A sintering strain rate of 10^-2 s^-1, controlled by applied pressure, maximizes the desired dual-phase stability.
A high-vacuum or Ar atmosphere prevents oxidation during processing.
High-energy milling introduces severe lattice distortion and a high density of dislocations.
Milling-induced defects increase the driving force and reduce the activation energy for solid-solution formation.
Severe deformation can kinetically retain a metastable single-phase or FCC-rich structure.
Rapid SPS uses stored deformation energy to densify the alloy at lower temperature and shorter time.
Short SPS exposure bypasses HCP and Laves phase formation because those phases require longer diffusion times to nucleate.
Local Ti compositional fluctuations produce a minor BCC phase while the matrix remains predominantly FCC.
The proposed process suppresses porosity and produces relative density above 98%.
The resulting alloy has a nanocrystalline grain size below 100 nm and an FCC-dominant structure with minor BCC.
The processed alloy exceeds 400 HV because of Hall–Petch grain refinement and solid-solution strengthening.
Eliminating brittle HCP and Laves networks permits elongation above 10%.
Temperatures above 1100 K or dwell times above 10 minutes cause HCP or Laves nucleation, grain coarsening, or phase segregation.
Ti contents above 20 at% can defeat kinetic suppression and cause HCP formation.
Nanoindentation at 10 mN with a 10 s dwell, compared only against a cast control, can test whether the hardness increase is attributable to grain refinement rather than solute strengthening.
The hypothesis is falsified by HCP above 10%, relative density below 95%, or a hardness increase no greater than 20% over the cast sample.

contradictions.description: The core regime requires a dwell time strictly below 5 minutes, but the proposed validation sample uses a 5-minute hold and nevertheless calls it a proposed-condition sample.
The hypothesis says phase stabilization requires a dwell below 5 minutes, whereas the boundary states that the hypothesis holds up to 10 minutes.
The predicted density is above 98%, but only density below 95% is declared falsifying, leaving results from 95% through 98% inconsistent with the prediction but non-falsifying.

The outcome attributes hardness to both grain refinement and solute strengthening, while the experiment claims to test grain refinement versus solute strengthening but uses only a cast control; this comparison does not isolate the two contributions.
